info.name: SRMS — DEMO (Assignment 2)
info.description:
Two runs in one collection.

**00 Setup** always first (it stores the two tokens and works out the booking dates).
**01 Core story** is the 12-request walkthrough that matches the demo script — enough for the video.
**02 Brief coverage** adds the rest of the Assignment 2 use cases (user management, menu administration, order editing, booking changes and cancellation, special events, the AI sentiment bonus). Run it when you want to show a bullet from the brief that the core run did not touch.

Before recording: `cd server && npm run db:reset && npm run dev`. Re-recording is fine without a reset: the pre-request script picks the next day the restaurant is open, and the booking requests use the table the availability query reports as free.

item.name: 01 Core story — the demo walkthrough
item.description: The shortest run that shows the design: sessions, server-side pricing, validation, the kitchen workflow, the double-booking guard, the assistant, the dashboard and the role check.

item.name: Browse the menu with SQL filters

request.description: The filter is SQL (JSON_CONTAINS on dietary_tags), not a JavaScript filter after the query.

item.name: Place an order (the server does the money)

exec: pm.test('the totals add up', () => { const o = pm.response.json().order; pm.expect(Number((o.subtotal + o.deliveryFee + o.tax).toFixed(2))).to.eql(o.total); });

request.description: Only ids and quantities are sent; tax and the delivery fee are added server-side.

exec: pm.test('the breakdown adds up to the headline', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); const sum = b.statusBreakdown.filter((r) => r.status !== 'cancelled').reduce((a, r) => a + r.revenue, 0); pm.expect(Number(sum.toFixed(2))).to.eql(b.orders.revenue); });

request.description: SQL aggregates — and the order and booking from a few requests ago are already counted.

item.name: 02 Brief coverage — the rest of the use cases
item.description: Run after 00 and 01 (it reuses their ids). One request per Assignment 2 bullet the core run did not show.

request.description: User management: bcrypt hash, then a token. A duplicate email would be a 409.
Customers see their own account; the password hash is never in the response.
Only whitelisted fields can be written.
Authorization: the owner or an administrator only.
The search runs in SQL; administrators can moderate accounts.

request.description: Menu management, the side of it the customer just failed.
Only one dish may be today's special — the previous one is switched off in the same transaction.
Order lines keep their own copy of the name and price, so history survives.
Add, remove and change quantities; the totals are recalculated from the database.
The line items come back with the prices paid at the time.
Scoped to the signed-in customer; an administrator gets every order.
Reservation management: view.
The table is re-checked against the new party size.
A cancelled booking frees the slot again, which is why the clash guard is a query and not a unique index.

request.description: Event management: the same booking rules, plus occasion, requirements and a menu selection.
The admin dashboard API also manages bookings and events, not only reports on them.
Explainable classifier: the rating plus a food-service lexicon, and each verdict reports why.
Local rules by default; ?provider=ai asks an external model and falls back if it is unavailable.
Reservation validation: the opening hours live in config and are checked on every booking.
User management, the last verb. Deleting the last administrator would be a 409.
